name: Engineers India Ltd
title: Engineers India Ltd - 532178 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Consultancy-led margin story: Q1 FY27 PBT up 55% to INR145 crore on consultancy segment profit of 24%, but turnkey revenue fell to INR302 crore from INR449 crore and order inflow was only INR514 crore against an INR8,000 crore annual target.

summary.headline: Engineers India Q1 FY27 standalone PAT rose 55% to INR109 crores, while turnover fell 7% to INR801 crores on Turnkey decline.
summary.overview: Standalone PBT rose about 55% YoY to INR145 crores and PAT to INR109 crores, helped by Consultancy growth of about 22% to INR499 crores. Turnkey turnover fell to INR302 crores from INR449 crores as major projects tapered. Order book stood at INR14,424 crores at 30 June 2026, but Q1 order inflow was only INR514 crores. Management kept the INR8,000 crore FY27 order inflow target and the FY27 operating margin guidance of 16%, and said the Middle East new-mega-project pipeline has slowed.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR104 crores, 11.72% in Q1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR14,424 crores (Consultancy INR10,498 crores; Turnkey INR3,926 crores)

segments.name: Consultancy & Engineering
segments.commentary: Turnover INR499 crores, up ~22% YoY; segment profit margin rose to ~24% from 17% in Q1 FY26, with management targeting 24-25%.

segments.name: Turnkey (LSTK)
segments.commentary: Turnover INR302 crores, down from INR449 crores as major projects tapered; segment margin ~7.5% in Q1 FY27. New Turnkey orders are in early execution, with turnover expected to rise in Q3 and Q4.

segments.name: CEIL subsidiary
segments.commentary: Profit INR6.88 crores vs INR2.69 crores a year earlier.

segments.name: Joint ventures / associates
segments.commentary: Contributed INR42.51 crores to consolidated profit vs a loss of INR7.37 crores in Q1 FY26. RFCL contributed about INR42 crores of revenue-linked profit; management expects some dividend from RFCL this year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow target of INR8,000 crores maintained; management said it will try to cross it. Current inflow is about INR2,750 crores (about INR1,100 crores overseas, about INR1,500 crores domestic, of which ~INR1,500 crores domestic is LSTK and the rest consultancy).
FY27 consultancy revenue targeted at more than 50%, possibly around 55%, implying consultancy turnover of INR2,300-2,400 crores.
Total FY27 turnover growth target of at least 10% on last year's INR3,850-4,200 crore base; management said guidance could improve.
FY27 operating margin target held at 16%, same as FY26; upside possible if pending change orders are settled.
FY28 revenue target of INR5,000 crores maintained, with an intent to improve it.
Dividend payout of around 100% for the current financial year referenced.
capex_capacity: Company is setting up a CBG plant with its own investment (non-hydrocarbon).
RFCL plant expected to run about 330 days a year; a 30-35 day regular shutdown in December will carry technical work without hitting profitability.
No specific capex amounts or commissioning dates were given for other projects.
demand_pricing: Middle East: new mega projects on hold or slow; existing jobs continuing. Secured about INR500 crores of Middle East business in Q1, including PMC work of INR400 crores under long-term agreements. Aramco contract in place but no major inquiry yet.
Overseas share of current inflow is about INR1,100 crores out of INR2,750 crores.
Nuclear: environmental studies for 3 private projects and 1 government project; engaged with NPCIL on engineering consultancy; SMR work secured last year.
Coal gasification: government VGF support of INR34,000 crores revived feasibility inquiries; an NTPC gas-to-SNG project is ongoing; results expected in a couple of months.
Domestic pipeline: BPCL Andhra execution tender may come by year-end; IOCL Paradip Phase 2 awaits OMC approval; ONGC petrochemical project only at feasibility stage.
Infrastructure about 45% of business in the current year, mostly LSTK/OBE, with a recent data-centre assignment from PowerTel.
Competition described as high in all segments, with most work won through competitive bidding.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR8,000 crore order inflow target still achievable, and how much would be consultancy?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the target is unchanged, with about INR2,750 crores in hand now and about two quarters left. Consultancy is about INR1,100 crores of this, with the rest mainly LSTK domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Will there be write-backs or change orders this year, including HPCL Barmer?
qa_highlights.answer: No exceptional change order is in the current quarter and no provision write-backs are expected; provisions reverse only after the defect liability period ends.

qa_highlights.question: How should consultancy growth and margins be modelled for FY27?
qa_highlights.answer: Consultancy growth target is at least 10%+ overall, with consultancy above 50% of turnover; segment profit is targeted at 24-25%. Operating margin target is 16%, with possible upside from change orders.

qa_highlights.question: Have Middle East clients put projects on hold due to the conflict?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no existing project is stopped; new mega projects are on hold or slow, and routine jobs continue.

qa_highlights.question: How will revenue be recognised on the Dangote Nigeria order?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue is recognised on cost-progress basis, with turnover booked as cost progress is achieved over about 4 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any plan to distribute surplus cash?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no plans to distribute the full reserves now, as other investment plans are under consideration, and pointed to about 100% dividend this year.

risks_watch: Turnkey turnover fell 33% YoY; management expects recovery in Q3-Q4 but this depends on execution of new projects still in early phase.
Q1 order inflow of INR514 crores is far below the run rate needed for INR8,000 crores; the target depends on a few lumpy domestic and overseas wins.
Middle East (about 12-15% exposure per analyst estimate) faces slow new mega-project awards; Saudi/Aramco work still at initial discussion stage.
Q1 operating margin of ~14% is below the 16% full-year target, so the guidance depends on later quarters and change-order settlements.
Coal gasification and nuclear inquiries remain at feasibility or EOI stage; timing and value of awards unclear.
Management did not confirm the Turnkey-to-consultancy mix beyond ranges given, and gave conflicting statements on the consultancy share (50-60%, around 55%).
summary.management_tone: Confident on consultancy margins, growth and dividends, but cautious on the Middle East and on new mega-project awards. Several answers were vague or shifting, notably on the consultancy mix, the margin target and the order-inflow path.
key_quotes: Company order book position stands at INR14,424 crores as on 30th June 2026, which comprises consultancy segment of INR10,498 crores and Turnkey segment constitute of INR3,926 crores.
New mega projects are under hold. Yes.
Definitely, it is the strategy of the company to keep consultancy business on higher side since we are having margin -- strong margin in the consultancy segment.
This year, we are targeting the operating margin of 16%, which we have achieved the last year also.
But as of now, there is no such plans to distribute the entire reserves to the shareholders.
